Let's carefully verify Kipchoge's record-making marathon pace and calculate the duration. Wait, what is Kipchoge's marathon record / pace? Let's see: Kipchoge's marathon world record is 2:01:09 (2 hours, 1 minute, 9 seconds) set at the 2022 Berlin Marathon! Wait, or is it 2:01:39? His personal best official world record was 2:01:09 (Berlin 2022). Wait, what about his sub-2-hour marathon time of 1:59:40 in the INEOS 1:59 Challenge (unofficial)? Or 2:01:09? Or 2:01:39? Let's check if there are other potential interpretations or if we should check both or calculate pace for all of them! Wait, let's write a python script to compute the hours and thousands of hours for all possible values: 1) World Record: 2:01:09 = 2*3600 + 1*60 + 9 = 7269 seconds for 42.195 km. Speed = 42.195 km / 7269 s = 0.00580478745 km/s = 20.89723483 km/h. 2) World Record: 2:01:39 = 2*3600 + 1*60 + 39 = 7299 seconds for 42.195 km. Speed = 42.195 / 7299 km/s = 20.811344 km/h. 3) INEOS 1:59 Challenge: 1:59:40.2 = 7180.2 seconds for 42.195 km. Speed = 42.195 / 7180.2 km/s = 21.156235 km/h. What about distance (Moon's minimum perigee)? From the Wikipedia Moon page infobox: `| periapsis = {{gaps |362 |600}} km
({{gaps |356 |400}}–{{gaps |370 |400}} km)` Text says: `The distance between the Moon and Earth varies from around 356,400 km (perigee) to 406,700 km (apogee)` So minimum perigee value on the Wikipedia page for the Moon is 356,400 km! Wait, is there any other value mentioned on Wikipedia for minimum perigee, e.g., 356,375 km or 356,353 km or 356,400 km or 356400 km? Let's check all perigee mentions on the Moon page and Orbit of the Moon page! Let's run a python script to test all combinations of these numbers! ```python cmd = """python -c " # Moon minimum perigee values from Wikipedia: # Infobox / text: 356,400 km (or 356400) perigee_km = 356400.0 marathon_km = 42.195 records = { '2:01:09 (2022 WR)': 2*3600 + 1*60 + 9, '2:01:39 (2018 WR)': 2*3600 + 1*60 + 39, '1:59:40.2 (INEOS)': 1*3600 + 59*60 + 40.2, '1:59:40 (INEOS)': 1*3600 + 59*60 + 40, } for label, sec in records.items(): speed_km_h = marathon_km / (sec / 3600.0) time_hours = perigee_km / speed_km_h thousand_hours = time_hours / 1000.0 rounded_thousand_hours = round(thousand_hours) rounded_hours_to_1000 = round(time_hours, -3) print(f'{label}:') print(f' speed: {speed_km_h:.6f} km/h') print(f' total hours: {time_hours:.3f}') print(f' thousand hours: {thousand_hours:.6f}') print(f' rounded to nearest 1000 hours: {int(rounded_hours_to_1000)}') print(f' thousand hours rounded: {rounded_thousand_hours}') " """ res = await run_command(cmd) print(res) ```
